question_text: The shaded region has area $0.42\text{ units}^2$. Find $k$, correct to 2 decimal places.

subparts.stem: The shaded region has area $0.42\text{ units}^2$. Find $k$, correct to 2 decimal places.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up the definite integral $\int_0^k \sin x\,dx = 0.42$

subparts.solution: $\text{Shaded area} = 0.42\text{ units}^2 \implies \int_0^k \sin x\,dx = 0.42 \implies [-\cos x]_0^k = 0.42 \implies -\cos k + \cos 0 = 0.42 \implies -\cos k + 1 = 0.42 \implies -\cos k = -0.58 \implies \cos k = 0.58 \implies k = \cos^{-1}(0.58) \approx 0.95 \quad \{2\text{ d.p.}\}$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The area under a curve is given by the definite integral; setting this equal to a given value solves for a boundary parameter.
step_by_step: Set up the area integral $\int_0^k \sin x\,dx = 0.42$.
Evaluate at the limits: $(-\cos k) - (-\cos 0) = 1 - \cos k = 0.42$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting that $-\cos(0) = -1$, leading to a sign error in $1 - \cos k$.
